name: Liang–Barsky parametric segment clipping
definition: For a=(x₀,y₀), b=(x₁,y₁), d=b−a and rectangle [L,R]×[B,T], set p=(−dₓ,dₓ,−dᵧ,dᵧ), q=(x₀−L,R−x₀,y₀−B,T−y₀). If any pᵢ=0 with qᵢ<0 reject. Otherwise ℓ=max({0}∪{qᵢ/pᵢ:pᵢ<0}), u=min({1}∪{qᵢ/pᵢ:pᵢ>0}). Reject if ℓ>u; else return (a+ℓd,a+ud)
variables: a,b ordered segment endpoints; d displacement; L,R,B,T inclusive rectangle bounds; p,q four coefficient pairs; ℓ,u feasible parameter limits
assumptions: Finite planar coordinates, L≤R and B≤T; closed rectangle and closed segment; exact arithmetic in mathematical definition; zero-length segments and degenerate rectangles allowed
limitations: Constant time and working storage for four inequalities; floating-point near-parallel or boundary comparisons can be unstable; no arbitrary nonconvex clip regions or measured performance advantage; identical returned endpoints represent a point
failure_conditions: Nonfinite coordinates, reversed bounds, unguarded division by zero or arithmetic overflow
computation: Initialize ℓ=0,u=1; skip each zero coefficient if its q is nonnegative, otherwise reject. Negative p raises lower bound, positive p lowers upper bound. Reject when lower exceeds upper. Map surviving interval endpoints into Cartesian coordinates; retain boundary tangencies

source.citation: University at Buffalo, CSE 480/580, Lecture 9, slides 6–8 (page images reviewed): parametric inequalities and interval updates. Slide 7–8 left coefficient sign inconsistency and missing parallel skip in pseudocode resolved algebraically from slide 6. https://cse.buffalo.edu/faculty/walters/cs480/NewLect9.pdf

application: General mathematical computation on synthetic or authorised inputs; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Two finite 2D endpoints, ordered finite rectangle bounds, arithmetic preserving comparisons
incompatible_methods: Treating a mathematical specification as an implemented or validated algorithm
mechanism_note: Parameter-interval clipping replaces repeated outcode endpoint replacement, but computes the same closed rectangular segment intersection as Cohen–Sutherland; classified as a variant, not additional independent scientific evidence

name: Scanline even–odd polygon filling
definition: For each selected integer row y, take every polygon edge (a,b) with min(aᵧ,bᵧ)≤y<max(aᵧ,bᵧ), and compute x=aₓ+(y−aᵧ)(bₓ−aₓ)/(bᵧ−aᵧ). Sort the resulting multiset x₁≤…≤x₂ₖ. Emit all integer pixel centers (x,y) with x₂ⱼ₋₁≤x<x₂ⱼ for j=1,…,k
variables: a,b adjacent vertices; x,y Cartesian pixel-center coordinates; k half the crossing count; n polygon edge count; H number of selected rows; M number of emitted pixels
assumptions: Simple closed nonzero-area polygon with finite vertices, implicit closing edge and no zero-length edges; integer pixel centers; horizontal edges excluded; lower-inclusive upper-exclusive edge activity and left-inclusive right-exclusive spans are explicit catalogue conventions; retain multiplicity of coincident crossings
limitations: Direct per-row intersection and sorting costs O(Hn log(n+1)+M) time and O(n) working memory excluding output; no active-edge-table performance claim; boundary rule is not closed-set containment; no antialiasing, holes or self-intersections in this specification; floating-point ordering near vertices requires care
failure_conditions: Invalid polygon, nonfinite coordinates, invalid row range or odd crossing count under stated assumptions
computation: For each row in the requested finite integer range compute and sort eligible intersections; assert even cardinality; pair consecutive crossings and emit integer x from ceil(left) through ceil(right)−1; zero-width pairs emit nothing

source.citation: Harriet Fell, Northeastern University CS 4300, Lecture 9, September 2011, slides 5–10 (extracted text reviewed; page-image requests returned HTTP 429). Parity and paired crossing approach; direct recomputation and lower-inclusive/left-inclusive boundary rules explicitly specified here rather than reproducing the lecture's endpoint preprocessing. https://www.khoury.northeastern.edu/home/fell/CS4300/Lectures/CS4300F2011-9-ScanLineFill.pdf

application: General mathematical computation on synthetic or authorised inputs; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Valid simple planar polygon, finite integer row range and exact or robust geometric arithmetic
incompatible_methods: Treating a mathematical specification as an implemented or validated algorithm
mechanism_note: Rowwise sorted edge intersections produce raster spans rather than evaluating individual point winding numbers; parity is related to containment but scanline batching and raster boundary policy are distinct computational procedures
